headline: All majors below the 200-day line; funding elevated on alts while BTC ETF bid persists; whales rotating ETH onto exchanges as shorts get liquidated.
paragraphs: The regime is firmly bearish across the board. All seven majors trade below their 200-day simple moving averages, and no golden crosses have printed. Bitcoin sits at 64,890, nearly 48 percent off its 12-month high of 124,739. Ethereum is worse at 60 percent down from 4,817. The rest of the major alts are between 53 and 79 percent underwater. This is not a market in a recovery trend; it is one testing whether recent momentum can hold above consolidation lows. The 90-day range shows Bitcoin trading between 58,566 and 81,059, Ethereum between 1,566 and 2,282. Price is clinging to the lower third of both bands.

Momentum tells a mixed story against that backdrop. Bitcoin's RSI stands at 54.5, neutral, with MACD above signal line: a tentative bid without conviction. Ethereum's RSI is 56.7 but MACD is below signal, a divergence that says the bounce lacks follow-through. BNB shows the sharpest momentum at RSI 64.2 with MACD above signal, the only major asset showing textbook positive momentum, though even BNB is down 53.9 percent from its high. XRP is the weakest at RSI 39.6, below 40 and MACD below signal, a signal that downside pressure persists. ADA's RSI reads 64.5, overbought on a local basis, but that is built on a 35 percent monthly gain and a 15.27 percent weekly pop off a deeply depressed base, not on trend reversal. The tape says resting momentum, not accelerating conviction.

Funding markets are the tension. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding rate sits at 0.14 percent annually (0.0014 percent per 8 hours), peacefully cheap. Ethereum's is 2.7 percent annualized, elevated but not panic territory. The problem children are the alts: SOL, XRP, and DOGE are all pricing 11 percent annualized funding, a tier above where you see it in strong trends. Those elevated rates suggest longs are paying to hold, a sign that positioning is crowded relative to conviction. The long-to-short ratio reinforces that: Bitcoin's is 1.16, Ethereum's is 1.34, but SOL sits at 2.15, XRP at 3.68, and DOGE at 4.65. These are extremely skewed toward longs. When liquidations paint the picture, shorts are getting flushed on ETH and SOL, with ETH shorts liquidated at 1.7 million against 405,000 for longs over the last 22 hours. XRP longs are also getting hurt, with 327,715 in longs liquidated versus 20,977 in shorts over 24 hours. Open interest is ample: Bitcoin has 2.02 billion on OKX, Ethereum 1.28 billion, SOL 239 million. The leverage ladder is full and lopsided.

Spot flows show institutional bid but fragmentation underneath. Bitcoin ETFs took in 101.7 million on August 7th, with all five recent sessions in the same direction for a 865-million inflow over the last five days. That is a real institutional bid. Ethereum ETFs added 49.6 million on the same date, 243.7 million over five sessions but only four days in the same direction. Over the last 48 hours, however, whales moved a net 302.6 million onto exchanges, with the headline driven by a massive 309.7-million inflow of Ethereum. The biggest single move was 165.7 million of ETH flowing to Coinbase retail. Bitcoin saw 388.1 million flow in but 395.2 million flow out, a near wash with slight net outflow of 7.1 million, though the biggest specific moves were 117.9 million off Kraken and holdings on cold storage. The picture is not uniform: ETH is moving onto exchanges while Bitcoin whales are selectively exiting. Stablecoins sit at 306.2 billion, down 1.03 percent over 30 days, flat supply. The crowd's dry powder is not shrinking but is not building either.

Sentiment remains in Fear at 31, within its recent 30-day range of 22 to 33, neither capitulation nor stability. The Fear-Greed gauge reflects the regime correctly. What does not reflect optimism is the liquidation picture: Bitcoin saw 186,181 liquidated in shorts against 128,379 in longs over 22 hours, a sign shorts are covering into the weak bounce. Ethereum saw 1.7 million in shorts flushed against 405,950 in longs. When shorts get blown out at this scale, longs are not in control; they are overextended relative to the actual support. The gap between funding (expensive on alts, tight on Bitcoin) and the actual direction of whale flows (ETH onto exchanges, Bitcoin flat) is the most honest read: longs are leveraged to the hilt on altcoins while smart money hedges exposure by liquidating into bids.

Watch for a funding collapse on the alts, particularly SOL and XRP, as the simplest signal that the positioning unwinds. Watch Bitcoin's 50-day simple moving average against the 200-day; they have not yet crossed above, and reclaim of that level would be the first textbook bullish signal in the daily structure. Watch whether ETH inflows to exchanges continue or reverse back to outflows; the current whip suggests indecision among large holders. Bitcoin network difficulty is retracting by 1.1 percent ahead of retarget at block 1920, a mild signal of miner capitulation or capital reallocation, but not yet severe. Total market cap moved 0.02 percent over 24 hours and Bitcoin dominance sits at 56.6 percent, stable. The tape is resting, overstretched on leverage, and waiting for a directional commitment.
